exposure: Maternal pure iron supplementation during pregnancy
Offspring iron supplementation (iron droplets) during the first 18 months of life
cohort: The study included up to 257 children with T1D (cases) identified from the Danish National Birth Cohort through linkage with the Danish Childhood Diabetes Register, and a larger cohort (n = 68,497) with maternal iron supplement data from the Danish National Birth Cohort.
finding: Maternal iron supplementation during pregnancy was not associated with later risk of T1D in offspring, but offspring intake of iron droplets during the first 18 months of life was inversely associated with the risk of T1D.
followup_time: Through childhood (up to diagnosis of T1D, prevalence 0.37% suggests observation into childhood years, though exact end age isn't specified, the exposure 'first 18 months' implies follow-up beyond this).
